articles.title_orig: Israeli Tanks Advance Across Gaza Cease-Fire Line in Rare Incursion
articles.title_zh: Israeli Tanks Advance Across Gaza Cease-Fire Line in Rare Incursion
articles.content_orig:
Dozens of displaced Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central ‌Gaza on Wednesday as Israeli tanks advanced, in what the Israeli military said was an operation targeting Hamas infrastructure outside areas that Israel controls in ⁠the enclave.
Witnesses said some Israeli tanks rolled onto the main Salahudeen road, west of the Yellow Line that marks the boundary of the two-thirds of the Gaza Strip still under Israeli control despite ⁠a ceasefire that has ​lasted more ⁠than a year.
An Israeli airstrike near the army raid killed one person, Palestinian medics said.
The medics ⁠said separate Israeli airstrikes had killed two other people ​earlier ⁠in the day in ‌ Deir al-Balah and Gaza City.
An Israeli military spokesperson told NBC News that the military was carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of ‌the Yellow Line in central Gaza ‌and that it had struck a militant in southern Gaza earlier on Wednesday.
They later confirmed that it was the first ground operation since the U.S. brokered ceasefire came into effect in October 2025 .
Dozens of Palestinians, most of whom have been displaced multiple times since the start of the war in 2023, piled their belongings on top of bicycles, wheelchairs, motorcycles and vehicles as ​they fled the area.
Salam Aql said the military had ordered residents of the area to leave “but we wanted to stay because we ​are exhausted from being displaced so many times.”
“We are tired, I swear to God, we are tired. But as we were sitting there, gunfire started ‌coming ⁠in,” she said, adding that a boy was hit in the leg by a bullet.
“Once he was wounded, we could not stay any longer.”
Hamas said the Israeli military’s raid and forced displacement of Palestinians marked a ceasefire violation and a ​dangerous escalation.
The truce halted major fighting in the Israel-Gaza war, although it has not stopped Israeli attacks or secured Hamas’ disarmament.
The Israeli military spokesperson had no immediate comment on other strikes.
Residents reported hearing tank shells being fired in the area. An Israeli airstrike near the location of the army raid killed one person, Palestinian medics said.
Israel, which says Hamas has recently been regrouping and rearming, has stepped up attacks against the Islamist group. Hamas has accused Israel of attempting to derail the U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement.
Gaza health ‌authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been ​killed since the ceasefire went into effect, while ‌the Israeli military says five Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Palestinian authorities say more ⁠than 74,000 people in Gaza have been killed in the military campaign ‌that Israel ​launched there after Hamas-led fighters killed ‌about 1,200 people in southern ​Israel in an attack on October 7, 2023.
The body overseeing US President Donald Trump’s plan to end the Gaza war on Wednesday ​accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ‌ceasefire in danger of collapse.
The 12-page Board of Peace report, seen by Reuters, is the body’s second to the United Nations Security Council since the US-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then.
The board, established and headed by Trump, is expected to present the report’s findings to a meeting of the council in New York at ​the end of November.
“The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” ​the report said, warning that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely.”
While the ceasefire has halted major ⁠fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect ​last year.
Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected the ​roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas is dismantled.
Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops.
“Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas’ agreement to the roadmap to the test,” the report said.
“Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ​been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble.”
Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”, accusing the ​Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to continue its aggression in Gaza.
The office of Israeli Prime Minister ‌Benjamin Netanyahu ⁠and a spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Chantal Da Silva reports on world news for NBC News Digital and is based in London.

articles.title_orig: El Salvador’s president confirms and celebrates attack on home of key Haitian gang leader
articles.title_zh: El Salvador’s president confirms and celebrates attack on home of key Haitian gang leader
articles.content_orig:
Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country.
On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”.
Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence.
The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti.
But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found.
“If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said.
That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay.
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge.
“The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday.
He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years.
“During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week.
The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead.
Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions.
Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations.
The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security.
Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials.
His heavy-handed approach has led to a sharp decline in crime but has also been widely condemned for human rights abuses.
Critics have warned that transplanting such tactics to Haiti could spark a backlash, leading to greater instability and risks to civilians.
They have also criticised the lack of long-term planning for El Salvador’s troop deployment; a sudden withdrawal, for instance, could worsen the situation for Haiti’s security forces.
Bukele is campaigning for a third term in El Salvador’s February presidential election, and analysts speculate his actions in Haiti could be used as a campaign tool to drum up support.
The Salvadoran deployment is the latest in a series of international interventions in Haiti.
Such foreign involvement is often controversial. The United States, for instance, has sent troops to Haiti on multiple occasions in the 20th century, occupying the country for decades and seizing control of its central bank.
More recently, a United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) arrived in Haiti in April, to help address the widespread gang violence.
Gangs control more than 80 percent of the capital region. The conflict has killed more than 22,000 people since 2022. UN reports attribute more than half of the deaths in the first nine months of the year to security operations, including the deaths of 300 civilians.
The UN also says almost 2,000 people have been displaced since the arrival of Salvadoran troops.
But Pelissier said Haiti’s government had not reported any civilian casualties in the latest operations, which he described as professional.
“The best to do is to avoid, as much as possible, human rights violations, and that’s what we are doing together,” the minister said.

articles.title_zh: Nasdaq rises in choppy trade as investors weigh Nvidia outlook, Anthropic IPO
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress gets an "A" for the financial performance and a "C" for the optics displayed on Tuesday's late-evening earnings call. New chair Harvey Jones — whom most Nvidia faithful have never heard of or from — gets a "C-" for his performance on the call.
The reality is Nvidia's leadership needs a better overall grade in the months ahead to sustainably win back market support.
Nvidia just put up another monster quarter, no doubt about it. Revenue and earnings easily topped expectations. Its outlook for the current quarter came in ahead of Wall Street estimates. Management pointed to approximately 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, up from the roughly 70% growth outlook then CEO Jensen Huang had previously discussed three months ago when he led the earnings call.
Let that sink in. Nvidia is talking about growing revenue at an extraordinary rate at a scale few companies in history have ever approached. Shares are up 2.5% on Wednesday in response.
There was more. The company cited a $2.5 trillion cloud backlog, expressed confidence that its next-generation chips will be released on schedule, and signaled that aggressive share repurchases will continue.
"FY28 underwritten as concern on near-term is largely addressed," Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley said.
But then there was the earnings call itself. And this is where things went astray.
This was Colette Kress's moment. The veteran Nvidia CFO is now Nvidia's interim CEO, stepping into a role that suddenly carries enormous weight following the leadership upheaval surrounding the disgraced Jensen Huang.
Yet the call felt strangely detached from the magnitude of what is happening inside the company.
Eight analysts asked questions. Not one mentioned Jensen's name. That was in part because Nvidia stonewalled them at the start of the call by saying it wouldn't answer any Jensen questions. This was tone deaf by Jones and Kress, and the analyst community did a horrible job of adhering to such bullshit from the world's most important stock.
Kress didn't mention his name either. Not once.
I found that remarkable. This is the man who founded Nvidia in 1993, helped build the products driving today's results, and became the face of the global AI revolution. The quarter being discussed was built on years of work under his intense leadership. The products shipping over the next 18 to 24 months will largely reflect that legacy too.
You don't have to turn an earnings call into a tribute to acknowledge reality.
Jones stumbled over remarks that sounded like he was reading from a fast-moving teleprompter. Maybe he is rusty at being in the public spotlight after years of yachting and home renovation work in his town of Nantucket, as this new profile would suggest .
Jones and Kress also leaned heavily on prepared remarks when addressing employees and the leadership transition. The message was essentially that employees remain committed and the company will take care of them. Fine. But investors deserve more than carefully rehearsed reassurances at a moment like this and in the wake of once-teflon Nvidia shares being down almost 30% in a month.
There was another important clue buried in the call: Kress sounded more measured about Nvidia's financial support for the so-called neocloud companies, including CoreWeave ( CRWV ). Nvidia has been an aggressive financial backer of parts of this AI ecosystem. Kress's comments suggested a more disciplined approach could be coming.
That matters. Nvidia needs customers with real businesses, real cash flows, and the ability to pay for the enormous amounts of computing infrastructure they are buying. The AI boom cannot run forever on circular financing and promises.
So here's where I land: The stock's initial positive reaction makes sense. The numbers were powerful. The demand outlook was explosive, as Kress characterized it. Nvidia is still an extraordinary business. But the company has a leadership problem to solve that quarterly revenue and profit beats cannot fix.
"We remain Sector Weight [rated], as uncertainty regarding who Jensen's successor will be likely keeps the stock range-bound," KeyBanc analyst John Vinh said.
Kress is a capable, experienced executive. She knows the numbers better than almost anyone. Nvidia clearly needs a permanent CEO who can combine technical credibility, strategic vision, and the kind of public-facing salesmanship that made Jensen Huang such a force.
You aren't going to find another Jensen. The assignment is to convince Wall Street that Nvidia's future doesn't depend on one person.
On earnings day, the numbers said yes. The earnings call didn't quite get there.

articles.title_orig: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
articles.title_zh: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Healthcare stocks fell again on Wednesday after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed a new rule that would toughen oversight of Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and the health insurance marketplace.
Sagging shares of managed care providers weighed on the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ), bringing the blue-chip index to a session low. UnitedHealth Group stock ( UNH ), one of the Dow's largest components with a 4.32% weighting, fell by about 8%. Humana ( HUM ) dropped 8%. Cigna ( CI ) shares declined by over 2%. CVS Health ( CVS ), which is in the process of splitting up its retail and insurance businesses, fell 3%.
Read more: Medicare out-of-pocket costs are rising in 2027
The rule, called the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare, or CRUSH, would increase audits of insurance providers and allow CMS to recover improper payments. It would also require providers to report changes to enrollment information within 30 days, among other conditions.
In the release shared on Monday, officials pointed to bad actors billing Medicare for nonexistent wheelchairs, enrolling healthy seniors in Medicare-funded hospice care, and signing people up for Marketplace plans without their consent as examples of the kinds of fraud this rule aims to crack down on.
CMS said the rule could save taxpayers nearly $90 billion over the next 10 years. The proposal is open to public comment until Jan. 19, 2027.
However, Oppenheimer analysts said they expect the proposal to face similar legal scrutiny to that of a framework a federal court struck down in 2025. Furthermore, the team noted that the $90 billion cost savings likely reflect CMS recouping repayments rather than broad savings to healthcare programs.
"We believe CMS will be subject to the same legal challenges that it faced in 2025," the analysts wrote. "The substantially larger collection estimate reflects broader auditing, with recoveries concentrated in 2028–2030. This is a proposed rule, so CMS could choose to make adjustments in the final rule. Even if the rule were implemented as is, and it were upheld by the courts, we believe plans would incorporate the prospective cost into bids rather than absorb an unchanged recurring earnings burden."

articles.title_orig: Lenovo Legion Go Beam handheld leaks ahead of CES 2027
articles.title_zh: Lenovo Legion Go Beam handheld leaks ahead of CES 2027
articles.content_orig:
Lenovo is reportedly preparing a cheaper Legion Go handheld for CES 2027.
Windows Latest has published three images of an unannounced Lenovo gaming handheld reportedly called the Legion Go Beam. The device appears to be a simpler alternative to the Legion Go 2, with fixed controllers, thicker display bezels and fewer controls. Its specifications are unknown, but the design suggests Lenovo may be preparing a more affordable model.
The leaked device resembles the Legion Go S, including its controller layout and front-facing speakers. However, Lenovo appears to have removed the touchpad and adopted a different arrangement for the USB-C and microSD ports. The white chassis also features green accents around the analog sticks and along the bottom edge. Unlike the Legion Go 2, the Beam does not appear to support detachable controllers.
The more interesting question is what processor Lenovo plans to use. We have previously reported on Intel’s lower-end Panther Lake handheld processors, including an eight-core configuration with four Xe3 GPU cores. The latest information points to a design with eight Efficient cores, although an earlier configuration featured four Performance cores and four Low Power Efficient cores. Either could potentially serve as the basis for a cheaper handheld, provided Intel proceeds with these designs.
AMD is another possibility. We previously covered reports of the Ryzen Z3 series, which is said to use Zen 6 CPU cores and RDNA4m graphics. With CES 2027 approaching, AMD could announce its next generation of handheld processors. However, that does not necessarily mean Lenovo would use the latest chip in a budget device.
There is also the possibility that Lenovo could continue using an older AMD design. The Ryzen Z2 lineup already includes the Z2 Go and Z2 A, based on Zen 3+ and Zen 2 architectures, respectively. AMD could follow a similar strategy with its next generation, keeping older silicon available for more affordable systems. At this point, there is no evidence linking the Legion Go Beam to any specific processor.
Windows Latest suggests Lenovo could introduce the device at CES 2027, where the company is scheduled to hold its Tech World event on January 6. There is no confirmation of its launch date, pricing or operating system. Both Windows 11 and SteamOS remain possibilities, as Lenovo already offers both platforms with its handheld lineup.

It went on to achieve enormous success, storming to the top of the Billboard Hot 100 chart and staying there for three weeks. articles.title_orig: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Return to Titanium
articles.title_zh: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Return to Titanium
articles.content_orig:
Apple's rumored "iPhone 20 Pro" could return to titanium as part of a more rounded design, according to the leaker known as " Fixed Focus Digital ."
In a new post on Weibo , the leaker said the iPhone 20 Pro will adopt a titanium frame with a more rounded design. A frame made of titanium is reportedly currently in use on prototype devices during early engineering work. They described the design as somewhat similar to the iPhone Air , but substantially more rounded.
If the claim proves accurate, it would mark a return to titanium for the Pro lineup. Apple used titanium frames for the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro, before switching to an aluminum unibody design with the iPhone 17 Pro in 2025. Apple highlighted aluminum's thermal conductivity as part of that redesign, which also introduced a vapor chamber to improve sustained performance.
While the change was praised for its improved thermals, light weight, and distinctive design, some users missed the more premium look and feel of titanium, along with its superior resistance to damage. The latest report regards development hardware, so it is still open whether titanium will be used in the finished product, but it seems plausible. The ‌iPhone Air‌ and iPhone Duo continue to use titanium frames.
The leaker's comparison with the ‌iPhone Air‌ builds on earlier claims about how Apple is developing the anniversary models. Earlier this week, Fixed Focus Digital said the devices would use the same glass material as the ‌iPhone Air‌, reshaped with greater curvature along all four sides.
An illustration accompanying that post depicted curved front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished metal frame. In August, Fixed Focus Digital claimed that Apple had modified iPhone Air manufacturing equipment to produce the more rounded glass components.
That combination of curved glass and a narrow metal frame is consistent with Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman 's reporting that Apple is planning front and rear glass panels that curve into the sides around a thin metal band . Gurman said an earlier, more ambitious version that replaced even more metal with glass had been abandoned during development.
The latest claim suggests titanium could form that remaining band. Gurman described the planned changes as the biggest overhaul of the Pro line since the iPhone X.
The extent of the curvature may still be under consideration. The leaker "Ice Universe" today claimed that Apple is developing four models with two different designs , including two with flat glass and two with glass that curves along all four edges. Apple has reportedly explored the curved design for three years, reducing the more pronounced curvature of earlier versions.
The curved models are said to have borders measuring around 1mm, with the surrounding glass making them appear almost invisible when viewed head-on. Screen protector samples circulating online offer a physical illustration of that approach, showing rounded corners, shallow curves along all four edges, and very narrow borders.
Alongside the changes to the glass and frame, the displays could grow slightly. The leaker "Digital Chat Station" has claimed that the Pro and Pro Max models will feature 6.41-inch and 6.96-inch screens , respectively, while also describing a four-sided curved design intended to appear borderless.
Separately, Ice Universe suggested that the main camera could gain a sensor with logic circuitry manufactured using a 17-nanometer process , potentially enabling faster readout speeds and improved power efficiency. The device could also lose the Action button and feature the "A21 Pro" chip based on TSMC's enhanced 2nm process (N2P).
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027. Leakers have referred to the devices as the "iPhone 20 Pro," but Apple's actual naming plans are unknown.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia's Chinese whispers reach Indian-American executive Jay Puri
articles.title_zh: Nvidia's Chinese whispers reach Indian-American executive Jay Puri
articles.content_orig:
Another short-seller is betting against Nvidia over problems it sees with alleged ties to China.
Muddy Waters, the activist short-seller run by Carson Block, unveiled a bearish bet ahead of the chip giant's earnings on Tuesday .
The firm's report centers around an ongoing class action complaint filed in October in California against Super Micro Computer, a company that makes servers and other hardware for AI systems. The suit claims that an executive named Cenly Chen had knowledge of illicit sales of Nvidia chips to China.
Muddy Waters points to Chen and a potential connection to former Nvidia executive Ajay Puri. The two have been photographed together numerous times over the years, though neither Muddy Waters' report nor the lawsuit directly accuse Puri or Nvidia of any wrongdoing.
"A woman identified as Cenly Chen, referred to in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, has been photographed in public between 2024 to 2026 with Ajay K. Puri. Until this June, Mr. Puri was likely the third most senior executive at NVDA, behind only Jensen Huang and Colette Kress," the firm's report reads.
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Super Micro Computer issued the following statement regarding Muddy Waters' report to Business Insider:
"Cenly Chen did not manage Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers," a spokesperson said. "After 18 years at Supermicro, Ms. Chen voluntarily resigned in early 2026 to take the CEO role at ChronoScale."
Muddy Waters said that Super Micro Computer did not respond to requests to confirm if the woman photographed was the same Cenly Chen who held roles at the firm, including as chief growth officer and managing director.
Super Micro Computer has come under legal scrutiny in the past. In March 2026, one of its co-founders was part of a group arrested for illegally smuggling AI chip components into China.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
"In March this year, the U.S. indicted three individuals associated with SMCI, including a co-founder, for illegally selling at least approximately $2.5 billion of SMCI servers with NVDA GPUs to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company," the Muddy Waters report states.
It added that a former Super Micro Computer executive stated in the lawsuit that there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge of [SMCI's] illicit sales."
This is the first time that Muddy Waters has announced a short position against the AI leader. The claims in its report aren't framed as wrongdoing on Nvidia's part.
At a time when investors are still focused on the fallout from Huang's alleged ties to Chinese tech executive Alice Huang, Puri's potential connection to Chen could raise more negative speculation as the chip leader tries to get back on its feet.
Muddy Waters CEO Carson Block said that his call is not based on a view of Nvidia's fundamentals or valuation. He told Business Insider he viewed the report as "our best shot at trying to get the company to go on the record and discuss if they have any knowledge of any issues there."
Nvidia did not discuss any of the details in Muddy Waters' report during Tuesday's earnings call.
The firm's report follows a short bet earlier this year revealed by Culper Research , which flagged many of the details that ended up turning into scandals for Jensen Huang this month, including his ties to Alice Huang and Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed.

articles.title_orig: Ford starts U.S. battery cell production using Chinese tech amid geopolitical tensions
articles.title_zh: Ford starts U.S. battery cell production using Chinese tech amid geopolitical tensions
articles.content_orig:
MARSHALL, Mich. — Ford Motor has started producing battery cells in the U.S. for its next generation of electric vehicles using technologies licensed by Chinese battery giant CATL.
The automaker said Wednesday that cell production at a $3 billion plant in Marshall, Michigan — roughly 100 miles west of Detroit — started last month and the cells are now shipping out. They'll be used in prototypes for its Fathom small electric pickup truck , which CEO Jim Farley has touted as rivaling Tesla and Chinese competitors.
The production marks a milestone for the Detroit automaker and is the next step toward using lower-cost lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, battery cells in U.S. vehicles. The technology was created in the U.S. but commercialized largely in China.
The automaker's decision to make the batteries at the roughly 2 million-square-foot facility has been criticized by some lawmakers and U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over Ford's ties to CATL.
Alan Clarke, Ford's vice president of advanced development projects, said licensing the technology from CATL helped the automaker bring the low-cost battery chemistry to the U.S. as quickly as possible.
"If we want to get to being able to produce affordable EVs in the United States, we need to also do it the fastest way possible," Clarke said Tuesday during a tour of the facility. "CATL being the biggest in the world means that they're the best supplier to get us that technology and help us learn ourselves how to produce LFP cells."
The U.S. government has increased scrutiny of Chinese ties with U.S. companies even as President Donald Trump is meeting this week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
In September, Duffy sent a letter to Farley expressing "profound concern" about Ford's ties to Chinese companies that it believes could be detrimental to the Detroit carmaker and the U.S. automotive industry. The White House a day later followed up by commending the automaker for its domestic jobs and manufacturing.
Ford — the largest producer of U.S. vehicles — has routinely touted its American roots, jobs and manufacturing, especially as the Biden and Trump administrations have pushed to onshore and grow U.S. production.
Ford's battery plant in Marshall is expected to be capable of producing 40 battery cells a minute, equating to 20 gigawatt-hours annually for EVs and the company's energy storage business. That's down from initial plans of up to 40 gigawatt-hours annually amid an EV pullback by the automaker and broader industry.
Ford has said the production pace will help reduce battery costs and that the facility has room for additional capacity if needed.
The facility is highly automated, but Ford said it's still in the early stages of certifying its processes, as it plans to ramp up cell production next year before the expected launch of the Fathom pickup during the fourth quarter of 2027.

articles.title_orig: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
articles.title_zh: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war
articles.content_orig:
There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground.
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
Going underground is now the "only option", says Zanuda, who has helped plan Ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard.
"On the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on."
The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground – accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.
Arriving at the tunnel entrance, the first thing to hit you is the lingering smell of gas and fetid air.
Both sides use openings in the pipeline to get to the surface, where most of the fighting takes place. They have made breaches in the ground, and used welding tools to break through the thick steel.
The Russians were the first to exploit the pipe to infiltrate the nearby city of Kupyansk in September 2025. They have used underground pipelines before, during the capture of the city of Avdiivka in 2024, and last year in their bid to recapture areas of Russia's Kursk region.
But Ukrainian forces have slowly turned the tables.
A specially designed electric cart transports troops and supplies through the pipeline.
They call it the Kupyansk metro. It occasionally breaks down. We travelled on it for 40 minutes, heads bowed and legs crossed. There is a regular bump as you cross the welded sections of the pipe. It is like an austere fairground ride, without the fun.
Our destination was a break in the pipeline where Ukrainian troops have built dug-outs to store ammunition and equipment, with just enough room to stand. It is where the man they call Musician conducts the movement of troops and supplies. He has been living like a mole, his face engrained with dirt and earth.
Musician tells me he has spent the past three months there, with a few brief visits above ground to clean up or go to the toilet. From time to time we can hear the thuds of artillery rounds above. Musician tells me we are close to the line of contact: "But it's safe underground."
The cart continues its journey into the bowels of the earth. It returns about half an hour later with more troops covered in dirt. They have been fighting in positions on the surface.
There is a look of relief on their dust-caked faces.
"It's more comfortable in the pipe because drones don't fly here, and neither do artillery shells or glide bombs," says Vovochka, who has been fighting on the ground for the past three weeks.
But there has been fighting in the pipeline, too. Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) along the pipeline.
It has been painstaking, backbreaking work – with the ever-present fear of coming into contact with the enemy.
Back above ground we meet a few of the soldiers, from the 13th Khartiia Brigade of Ukraine's National Guard, who have taken part in the mission. Their first task was to clear the detritus, water and Russian barricades inside the pipeline.
The Ukrainian troops say some of the barriers were boobytrapped or piled with Russian bodies. "When we moved them or climbed over them, we had no idea what was underneath," says Chyzh.
The other danger, he said, was the ricochets from gunfire when they tried to advance. "You never know where a bullet is going to go or how it will bounce."
His comrade Kort says "we were all firing, we were pushing them back". Over the course of the operation Ukraine says it killed more than 100 Russian soldiers and took 30 prisoners. "Yes, there were bodies," says Kort. "I even had to sleep right next to them."
Their commander's former life as a miner helped prepare them for the physical and psychological challenges of operating underground.
From a building on the surface, Biashym keeps in regular contact with his men still in the pipeline. Behind him is a cabinet full of medicine.
Soldiers in the pipeline spend much of their time on their knees and suffer abrasions. Biashym admits some have had panic attacks from living in such a confined space. Others have struggled to breathe.
Hundreds of Colombian volunteers have also been involved in the operation, part of the RUG 23rd Assault Regiment.
Foreign fighters have helped boost Ukraine's depleted ranks. One of the Colombians, whose call sign is Gecko, tells me it took them 30 days to just clear 500m.
"It was difficult, it was hot and I had fear inside the pipe," he said. "But at some point I just thought, OK, just deal with it and let's advance."
The battle of the pipeline is not over.
Russian forces, like Ukraine's, have built fortified positions inside the pipeline. They still try to infiltrate Ukrainian positions, burrowing their way in and out of the pipe. From a control room above ground we watched Ukrainian drones target another Russian attempt to outflank them.
While some of the fighting taking place underground, there are still battles on the surface and in the air. It has been a combined operation.
But Zanuda, who is chief of the planning section of the 13th Khartiia Brigade, believes it is the best way to fight in the future. "Ground operations are now nearly impossible," he said, adding that "everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground".
There'll be more missions like this, he believes. "Pipelines run everywhere," he said. "You have to remember, back in the Soviet times, oil, gas and ammonia were being transported to Europe, with the entire transit route running through Ukraine."
In reality it has been brutal, gruelling and dangerous work in the harshest of conditions.
It has taken Ukraine seven months to clear 15km of the pipeline.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed it as a success.
It has helped retake lost territory and been a boost for morale, but on its own it has not changed the course of the war.

United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend.
That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further.
"While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18).
This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.)
ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update.
Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit.
In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance.
Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure.
Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

articles.title_orig: NVIDIA GeForce driver bug may cause continuous SSD writes even at idle
articles.title_zh: NVIDIA GeForce driver bug may cause continuous SSD writes even at idle
articles.content_orig:
NVIDIA drivers 621.14 and 621.24 reportedly cause repeated SSD writes at idle.
Users are reporting excessive SSD write activity caused by NVIDIA GeForce drivers, just days after AMD released a fix for a similar problem. The issue reportedly affects the NVIDIA Display Container service, which may continuously write data to the system drive even when the PC is idle. Some users claim write activity reaching 30GB per hour.
According to reports collected by TroubleGrid and discussions on NVIDIA’s official forums, the process responsible is NVDisplay.Container.exe. The service repeatedly writes to a binary logging file named nvlog.nvlgstg , located in the NVIDIA Corporation directory under ProgramData. Rather than appending new information, the process reportedly rewrites the file, generating repeated disk operations.
Users have traced increased activity to GeForce driver 621.14, released on November 4. One comparison showed approximately 515MB of process-level writes during five minutes of idle time, compared with less than 2MB using driver 621.01. Another user reported more than 3GB in ten minutes, while a separate report involving driver 621.24 claims approximately 30GB per hour. These measurements represent reported process activity and do not necessarily correspond to the same amount of physical SSD writes.
It seems Nvidia GPU drivers also constantly write to your SSD by u/Remarkable_Fly_4276 in pcmasterrace
The problem may also affect systems with NVIDIA’s recording and overlay features disabled. Some users reported reduced disk activity after disabling ShadowPlay-related features, while others continued experiencing the issue. Similar complaints about NVIDIA’s background logging date back several years, suggesting the behavior itself is not entirely new.
Affected users can check disk activity through Windows Resource Monitor by opening the Disk tab and looking for NVDisplay.Container.exe. Some users have temporarily reduced writes by stopping NVIDIA Display Container LS, deleting the affected log file and restarting the service. Others report that reverting to driver 621.01 resolves the problem. Disabling the service permanently can interfere with NVIDIA Control Panel and NVIDIA App functionality.
AMD recently addressed excessive system drive writes with Adrenalin 26.11.1, released on November 12. NVIDIA has not publicly acknowledged the current reports, and its latest 621.24 driver release notes do not list the issue.
Source: TroubleGrid Wccftech

articles.title_orig: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
articles.title_zh: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night.
The announcement comes after Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO, should the board allow it. Huang abruptly resigned last week amid national security concerns and reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Jones said Nvidia’s board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent leader.
The company sought to reassure investors and offer clarity about its future in the third-quarter earnings report Tuesday evening, with Kress, saying Nvidia’s “roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.”
“Our ambition will not change, our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change,” Kress told investors, whose confidence in the company’s future has been badly shaken by the scandal , on the earnings call.
It’s the first financial picture investors are getting since the chipmaker was shaken last week by Huang’s resignation after three decades at the helm of the company he founded.
Nvidia more than doubled its quarterly revenue and profit from a year prior, and both figures beat Wall Street’s expectations.
Lies, spies and sex are just one part of the Nvidia story. The real stakes are much bigger
Nvidia’s earnings — the numbers and executives’ comments — have long been viewed as a bellwether for the larger AI industry, with Nvidia’s technology and funding at the heart of much of the boom. That’s especially true now with questions swirling about the industry’s future without Huang, its biggest cheerleader and dealmaker, at the helm.
Nvidia shares were coming off their worst week in 19 months heading into the report. The stock is down 16.7% since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair and Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, erasing $751 billion in market value. Since Nvidia shares hit their record high on October 6, they have dropped 35%, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market value.
Ahead of the report, Siebert Financial Chief Investment Officer Mark Malek wrote that it would be the “most important in the company’s history.”
Nvidia shares have dropped for four consecutive days since Huang resigned. Shares fell just 0.44% Tuesday. But shares moved higher in after-hours trading after the earnings release and analyst call, gaining roughly 5% as of 6:10 p.m. ET.
“The massive results, strong guidance and reassurance that the strategy Huang put in place remains firmly on track show that an orderly CEO transition does not necessarily have to dilute the company’s value,” Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com, said in emailed commentary following the release. He added that Nvidia’s growth train “can continue with or without Huang, provided the company makes the right call on leadership.”
Nvidia’s board said last week that Kress, the company’s CFO of 13 years, would serve as interim CEO as it considered internal and external candidates to permanently fill the role. Nvidia’s board also said Tuesday it had established a new national security and export control oversight committee to ensure the company is abiding by global trade regulations, and that it will strengthen its internal national security and compliance initiatives.
Some Nvidia employees, investors and other tech leaders had called on the board to reinstate Huang as CEO, pending the outcome of its investigation into his multiple reported extramarital affairs, including with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang , whom US officials suspect as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; and at least one direct subordinate at Nvidia.
Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided that his “return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America,” in his first public comment since resigning.
Jones said during Tuesday’s call that he would not take additional questions regarding Huang’s resignation or the company’s investigation, but that the board would “communicate further when appropriate.” Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company.
Meanwhile, Huang is set to testify on Capitol Hill on December 1. He is expected to face questions about his relationship with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s sales of chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which some US officials believed should have been labeled a national security risk.
Some US sources say that whether or not Alice Huang was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions.
Huang’s exit aside, concerns about whether the AI trade is a bubble about to burst, with valuations and infrastructure spending outpacing returns, had already begun to reach a fever pitch in recent months. Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN this week that he believes the AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election.
Nvidia’s Tuesday report indicates that, at least for now, the company’s growth continues to outpace Wall Street’s expectations.
The company posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% year-on-year. Profits reached more than $65 billion, up 105% year-on-year. Kress also said demand for the company’s next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology is “off to an explosive start,” with the tech already in use by customers such as Google, Microsoft and Oracle.
Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains strong, with a handful of the biggest AI and cloud companies expected to shell out more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures next year alone. But in the wake of Huang’s exit, investors have been more concerned with the company’s future business.
The report also comes after a blue wave in the US midterm elections ushered in a slate of newly elected leaders, many of whom campaigned on slowing or restricting data center development, which could dent Nvidia’s business.
Analysts with research firm IDC wrote in a report last week that the firm sees “near-term AI infrastructure demand and supply as largely locked in, so the harder questions,” like long-term bets on emerging technologies and the financing system that Jensen Huang sat in the center of , “sit further out.”
Nvidia said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to come in around $130 billion, plus or minus 3% — exceeding what Wall Street analysts had predicted, according to consensus estimates from FactSet.
Kress raised the company’s growth estimates for next year even higher from its already-ambitious targets, saying Nvidia’s revenue is expected to grow by 75% in fiscal 2028, up from 70% in the last earnings call.
Significant questions also remain about the future of Nvidia’s business in China, and potentially in Asia more broadly, as US officials react to the national security concerns surrounding the company.
Shipments of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China made up less than 1% of sales in its core data center business in the previous quarter . However, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15% of revenues when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.”

articles.title_orig: Trump Says the U.S. Will “Catch” China on Rare Earths Within 10 Months - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.title_zh: Trump Says the U.S. Will “Catch” China on Rare Earths Within 10 Months - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin .
It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.
He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit . Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents.
A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.
“China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said.
After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags.
Xi’s gesture Wednesday most likely reflects a desire by him and his government to “show respect to Trump,” which they know he enjoys, William Yang, a senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, said in a post on X .
“It is likely also an attempt to uphold the positive rapport between Xi and Trump ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations in the coming months,” he said.
When Trump last visited China in May, he was greeted at the airport in Beijing by Vice President Han Zheng.
Putin, who has a close relationship with Xi and has met with him 50 times as of Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader when he arrived earlier at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport. Putin was instead met by Cai Qi, a close Xi adviser and member of the Politburo Standing Committee.
Xi has met with a number of world leaders, including Putin, as they gather in Shenzhen this week for a summit of Asia-Pacific economies.
Trump, Putin and Xi are holding an unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the summit.
Ahead of his bilateral meeting with Xi on Wednesday, Putin said he expected “great potential benefits” from the trilateral talks, which have sparked anxiety in places such as Ukraine, Iran and the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan, where officials worry the world’s three most powerful leaders could make decisions about their futures without consulting them.
In a briefing last week, a senior U.S. official said the trilateral meeting was unlikely to produce any sort of agreement, describing it as an “entry point” and “the first conversation.”
Jennifer Jett is the Asia Digital Editor for NBC News, based in Hong Kong.
Erin Tan is a news researcher in NBC News’s Beijing bureau.

articles.title_orig: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
articles.title_zh: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
articles.content_orig:
ABC News has sidelined the staffers behind a botched report about alleged investments tied to President Donald Trump’s children. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto)
ABC News quietly suspended staffers involved in the botched story last month suggesting impropriety in the Trump sons' business dealings, Fox News Digital has confirmed.
The Disney-owned network stirred controversy with its report headlined, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election," alleging that Anduril, the company investing in a new Baltimore shipyard, had ties to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump through 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm. The report claimed the firm had a "major stake" in Anduril, which was ultimately false.
ABC News raised eyebrows when it deleted the report without explanation after the story was called out on social media, then quietly republished a revised version of the report with an editor's note acknowledging the error.
GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR FCC PROBE OF ABC NEWS OVER TRUMP SONS-ANDURIL 'POLITICAL HIT JOB'
1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. serves as a partner, has considered legal action against ABC News. (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images)
The ordeal resulted in an internal probe to determine what went wrong. While two staffers behind the botched story were reprimanded and rumors they will be terminated swirl, an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "No one's employment status has changed."
ABC News declined further comment.
The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported that the two staffers were on "paid leave."
ABC News' original story wrote, "1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company."
"Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov , the official system for government contracting," the story continued. "The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one."
ABC NEWS QUIETLY REPUBLISHES GUTTED VERSION OF STORY ON TRUMP SONS IT HAD DELETED WITHOUT EXPLANATION
President Donald Trump and his son, Trump Organization Executive Vice President Eric Trump. (Brendan Moran/Sportsfile via Getty Images)
Alexa Henning, a spokesperson for 1789 Capital and a former chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, took to social media, insisting the company does not have a "major stake" in Anduril and blasting the "biased hit piece."
"Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning reacted at the time .
"Meaning the ‘investments’ mentioned were actually the total number raised for a funding round, that MANY companies contribute to," Henning continued. "Another thing that the reporter buried the lead on was that many of these companies have gotten government contracts during Biden AND Trump, which completely negates the assertion by ABC that Don Jr and Eric Trump are doing anything wrong."
VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM TIED TO DONALD TRUMP JR WEIGHS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST ABC NEWS OVER BOTCHED REPORT
ABC News then sparked confusion among critics when it deleted the entire story, only to republish an overhauled version of the story days later with the new headline reading, "New shipyard announced amid earlier Democratic concerns about potential conflicts of interest" while stressing to readers that Trump Jr. "is not involved in investment decisions."
"CORRECTION: A version of this story published on Oct. 7 contained errors in the description of certain company investments, government contracts and event chronologies," the editor's note read at the top of the article. "After subsequent reporting, this version contains corrected information and additional context regarding some of those investments, contracts and events."
Henning has said that nobody from ABC News asked 1789 for comment prior to the initial story being published and that an ABC News journalist "vigorously defended" the report before it was suddenly deleted. She also previously said the company was considering legal action against the Disney-owned news organization.
"This should be a cautionary tale for any other reporters who continue to traffic in this false narrative," Henning told Fox News Digital on Wednesday when asked if a lawsuit is still being considered.

articles.title_orig: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why
articles.title_zh: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why
articles.content_orig:
Waymo is currently restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars’ driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times , this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.”
This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations.
In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.”
Waymo also told the government that the updated software is better able to respond to emergency vehicles when in a construction zone and that the company has made “operational changes that better identify and mitigate potential entry into pre-planned construction zones and enable more Remote Assistance capability” if it happens again.
Which it has. Despite the update to improve behavior around emergency vehicles, a video went viral in early November showing a Waymo robotaxi on I-280 driving past a pair of California Highway Patrol cars conducting a rolling roadblock as they held traffic behind a slow-moving construction vehicle. California also says there was an incident in which a Waymo robotaxi entered a construction zone on US 101 near Burlingame.
“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Waymo told Ars. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”
Waymo also told Ars it was continuing to work with the various California agencies that regulate transport.
Until the suspension, Waymo was only conducting highway operations in Los Angeles and the Bay Area in California, as well as in Arizona.

articles.title_orig: Iran attacks US air base in Kuwait
articles.title_zh: Iran attacks US air base in Kuwait
articles.content_orig:
Iran targeted a Kuwaiti air base that hosts US forces on Wednesday, widening the scope of its attacks after the US military hit what it said was a missile launch site in Iran.
Iran’s army targeted Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait with drones, state-run Press TV reported. The Kuwaiti Army’s General Staff said any explosions heard were caused by air defense systems intercepting incoming attacks.
Neighboring Bahrain, which is home to the US Fifth Fleet and has faced repeated Iranian attacks over the past week, also sounded air raid sirens early Wednesday, with the military saying it had intercepted “a number of Iranian aerial attacks” early Wednesday.
CNN has contacted the US Central Command (CENTCOM) for comment.
Just hours earlier, US fighter jets carried out a “self-defense” strike against an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island using “precision munitions,” according to an American military official.
The strike “was in response to IRGC aggression targeting American personnel and assets,” the official said, noting that CENTCOM remains “highly vigilant and fully postured to protect Americans across the region.”
Iranian state media reported that an area on the outskirts of a city on Qeshm Island had been targeted in an “enemy attack.” Ahmad Nafisi, the deputy governor of Hormozgan province for political and security affairs, said the strike caused no damage to vital infrastructure, commercial or residential areas.
Iran’s widening attacks come as Tehran warns it will not accept a prolonged stalemate in its war with the US, while President Donald Trump has signaled a preference for maintaining crippling economic pressure on the Islamic Republic rather than resuming full-scale hostilities. Iran has also threatened to expand the war significantly and warned that it will not wait for another US attack before striking.
Tuesday’s US strikes appear similar to others in recent weeks around the Strait of Hormuz, which US officials have also characterized as defensive, rather than marking a significant escalation by American forces.
A third US aircraft carrier strike group recently entered CENTCOM’s area of responsibility, where it is expected to — at least temporarily — join ongoing operations that include enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports and conducting escort operations for commercial ships willing to transit the Strait.
Attacks on oil and gas tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have surged in recent weeks. On Wednesday, the United Arab Emirates’ state-owned ADNOC energy company said one of its vessels had been attacked while transiting the waterway the previous evening, leaving 11 crew members injured and one missing.
“Today’s developments should serve as an important reminder of the inherent instability of the current situation,” Hamidreza Azizi, an Iran analyst at Crisis Group, wrote on X. “Some within the Trump administration – and perhaps even Trump himself – may believe that Washington can maintain economic pressure and the naval blockade against Iran indefinitely while avoiding another full-scale war. But the developments of the past 24 hours demonstrate how difficult it is to sustain such an arrangement.”
There is little indication of an imminent diplomatic agreement to end the conflict, and Trump has warned he could resume full combat operations if Tehran refuses to accept the US administration’s demands.
Trump was widely expected to hold off on restarting those combat operations until after the US midterm elections but appears to still be mulling over how to proceed, absent a last-minute deal.
With Democrats poised to take control of the House and Senate in January, Trump’s window to decide on a path forward in Iran appears to be shrinking. CNN has previously reported that it is likely untenable for the US military to maintain the status quo indefinitely, but only Trump has the power to decide when the war is over.
CNN’s Abbas Al Lawati, Lucas Lilieholm and Mohammed Tawfeeq contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Mexico Leader Goes Viral in China for 21-Hour Economy Flight
articles.title_zh: Mexico Leader Goes Viral in China for 21-Hour Economy Flight
articles.content_orig:
President Claudia Sheinbaum promoted Mexico as an investment destination in an address to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday.
In a 13-minute speech , she also touted Plan México — the federal government’s overarching economic and industrial policy — and spoke about a range of initiatives and achievements of her two-year-old administration.
Desde Shenzhen, China, les comparto mi participación en APEC CEO Summit 2026; en representación de México, expusimos a líderes económicos y empresarios del mundo que el desarrollo con bienestar es posible. https://t.co/3AEDA9Wve3
— Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 17, 2026
According to a Xinhua news agency article posted to a Chinese government website , the APEC CEO Summit 2026 brings together “business and political leaders from across the Asia-Pacific and beyond to discuss regional economic cooperation and future development.”
“Under the theme ‘To Prosper and Win the Future Together,’ the two-day event has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland,” the article says.
“Participants include representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, as well as heads of several international organizations and representatives of business associations from Russia, the United States and other economies.”
In addition to speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Sheinbaum will attend the APEC Leaders’ Meeting during her visit to Shenzhen. She arrived in the southern Chinese city on Monday and is scheduled to return to Mexico on Friday.
Promoting Mexico as a destination for foreign investment, Sheinbaum touted Mexican talent as well as the country’s geographic location and its trade agreements with other nations, among other competitive advantages.
“We have engineers. We are among the top five countries in the world in terms of the number of engineers produced. We have public universities, research centers, highly educated young people and a strong industrial tradition,” she said.
“We have the capacity to participate in major global value chains, but also to innovate and build strategic industries. We have a privileged geographic location, an extensive network of trade agreements, an economy integrated into the world’s major markets, natural resources, expanding infrastructure and, above all, the human talent of a hardworking people,” Sheinbaum said.
“Mexico guarantees conditions for investment, certainty and a long-term vision for development,” she said.
As part of Plan México, the federal government is seeking to attract more foreign investment to Mexico and strengthen and support the country’s vast manufacturing sector.
Foreign direct investment in Mexico reached a record high of almost US $35 billion in the first six months of 2026 , but the pace of year-over-year growth, at 2.1%, was not particularly strong.
By speaking at the APEC CEO Summit, Sheinbaum had the opportunity to court investment from major companies in APEC economies and beyond.
Three of Mexico’s five leading sources of foreign investment in the first half of 2026 are APEC members, namely the United States, Canada and Australia. Investment from China has increased in recent years , but the East Asian economic powerhouse was not among the top investors in Mexico last year .
Insecurity, uncertainty surrounding the future of the USMCA free trade pact — which the U.S. government has so far declined to extend to 2042 — and Mexico’s controversial judicial reform, which introduced the popular election of judges , are seen as among the factors discouraging investment in Mexico.
At the start of her address, Sheinbaum highlighted that Mexico is the world’s 11th most populous country and 13th largest economy.
“But above all, we are a nation with a history stretching back thousands of years, where Spanish is spoken, but so are 68 indigenous languages,” she said.
Sheinbaum went on to say that Mexico is building its “own” economic model with “roots in our history, our cultural greatness, and the strength, talent and capabilities of our people.”
“This transformation began in 2018. And starting in 2024, with the election of Mexico’s first female president, we gave it a new dimension through Plan México,” she said.
“Plan México is a vision for the nation. It is the decision to turn our capabilities, resources, strategic position, and talent into drivers of development grounded in sovereignty and social justice,” she said.
She said that the plan is based on “five principles,” namely “shared prosperity; energy and food sovereignty; public, private, and public-private investment in infrastructure; incentives for private investment; and environmental responsibility in the face of climate change.”
Sheinbaum also said that Plan México “has a humanist vision” in which “the economy is at the service of the people” rather than the other way around.
“For decades, it was argued that the wealth of a select few had to grow first, and that over time, the benefits would trickle down to the rest of society. In Mexico, we are proving that the path can be very different,” she said.
Sheinbaum said the government and private companies are expected to invest a total of US $432 billion in infrastructure under Plan México between 2024 and 2030.
“We are transforming the country’s productive capacity, connecting regions, bringing markets closer together, improving logistics, and creating jobs,” she said.
“At the same time, we are promoting investment in industry and services through incentives, certainty, streamlined administrative procedures, and new development hubs aligned with each region’s economic strengths. This has enabled us to become the fifth-largest economy in the world in terms of foreign direct investment,” Sheinbaum said.
In her closing remarks, she said she hadn’t traveled to China “just to offer investment opportunities.”
“We came to share a vision for the future,” she said.
“A vision in which Mexico grows and, at the same time, all economies become stronger and prosperity is a shared achievement,” Sheinbaum said.
In various ways, Sheinbaum’s address at the APEC CEO Summit was similar to her annual government report ( informe ) speeches, the most recent of which she delivered on Sept. 1 . The difference was that her speech in Shenzhen on Tuesday was delivered on the world stage and was directed at international businesspeople and leaders rather than a domestic audience.
In a vast auditorium in China’s tech capital, Sheinbaum acted as cheerleader in chief for Mexico, and also for the fourth transformation (4T) political project she leads. She highlighted that since Andrés Manuel López Obrador — the founder of the 4T — became president eight years ago, Mexico’s minimum wage has increased 154% in real terms and some 17 million people have been lifted out of poverty , according to World Bank data.
Sheinbaum also spoke about Mexico’s various social programs, and declared that her government is establishing a “ verdadero estado de bienestar ” — a phrase that can be read as a “true welfare state” or, more broadly, a country that prioritizes people’s well-being.
In addition, she highlighted her government’s major investment in highway, rail, electricity, water, port and housing projects.
Sheinbaum’s speech to the APEC CEO Summit came a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to address the event. Li Qingshuang , vice-chairperson of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, said on Sunday that leaders from 12 APEC economies, including Canada, Chile and South Korea, will attend the APEC CEO Summit and deliver speeches or remarks, or participate in panel discussions.

articles.title_orig: 8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2
articles.title_zh: 8BitDo Reveals Its Own GameCube Controller For Switch 2
articles.content_orig:
8BitDo, known for its work in providing excellent retro-inspired controllers for modern systems, has announced the GC Bluetooth Gamepad to celebrate the GameCube's 25th anniversary. It's currently scheduled to launch on 10th December 2026 .
Compatible with Switch, Switch 2, and Windows, the GC controller maintains the core shape and layout of the iconic GameCube pad, but adds in a bunch of modern upgrades like TMR sticks and Hall Effect triggers. Priced at $49.99 , it undercuts Nintendo's official offering by $20 and is available for pre-order now.
Colours include purple and orange, which are arguably the most recognisable from the original release (though we're hoping for a Wavebird-inspired silver variant in the future, too). The pad also features single-rotor rumble to replicate the feel of the original, while a new 'ZL' button – which also features on the official Nintendo GameCube pad for Switch 2 – has been designed to be symmetrical to the 'Z' button on the right.
While we do have a dedicated capture button, there unfortunately doesn't appear to be a 'C' button for chat purposes. It's also not clear at this stage whether the GC controller will have wake-up support for Switch 2, but 8BitDo has generally been pretty good at including this, even if it's not necessarily supported immediately at launch.
Here's an official list of features from 8BitDo:
- Classic GC design and iconic button layout - TMR joysticks with octagonal gates - Hall Effect linear triggers - Single-rotor rumble - Symmetrical Z and ZL bumpers - Capture button for screenshots and recording - Turbo function - Support for multiple simultaneous gamepad connections
Finally, it's worth noting that if you purchase the 8BitDo Retro Receiver for GC , you can use the new controller – or indeed the official GameCube pad – with original hardware.

articles.title_zh: Shelly’s new smart valve shuts off your home’s water before a leak becomes a flood
articles.content_orig:
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
After releasing a $28 leak sensor earlier this year that conveniently runs off a battery for two years, Shelly is announcing an accompanying smart valve you can install on your home’s main water line to automatically turn off the flow when one of those sensors detects a problem. The Shelly Neo Smart Water Valve is available now through the company’s online store for $499.99, plus the cost of installation if you don’t trust your plumbing skills. It’s not a cheap solution, but it’s cheaper than the fallout of a leak turning into a disaster.
The Neo Smart Water Valve is designed to be installed on a standard US 1-inch thread connection (the company plans to launch additional size options next year) and is made from brass so it’s safe to use on plumbing carrying drinking water. It has an IPX7 waterproof rating so the valve will keep working if flooding means it ends up submerged. However, the valve lacks a battery of its own and requires a connection to a power source through an included USB adapter cable. Connecting it to a waterproof power bank instead of an outlet may be the best approach to ensure it still works during a power outage.
The smart valve connects to other devices over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and is designed to integrate into existing smart home setups using webhooks, MQTT , or scripting for advanced users. In addition to shutting off the flow of water into your home in about 12 seconds, the valve also features an ultrasonic measurement system that tracks pressure, flow rate, your home’s consumption, and even the temperature of the water. Through the Shelly app, you can monitor all of that data in order to spot unusual usage patterns that could indicate a wasteful leak, or ensure the pressure doesn’t get high enough to damage pipes or appliances.
